title: A four-diagnostic linear rule lost to a family gate in five excluded climate-response families
abstract: Can training diagnostics select useful climate terms within a family better than a family gate? We fitted two linear decision rules on published model statistics from 20,942 series in 11 families. We used nested family holdouts to select penalties and excluded a later study with five families and 11,791 series from fitting. The four-diagnostic rule used cross-validated climate signal, a forward training backtest, trailing-mean skill and residual correlation. Its mean bounded error advantage over the trailing mean was 0.0073 in the excluded study. A signal-only fitted rule gave -0.0425, and a trend-aware family gate gave 0.0377. The four-diagnostic rule lost to that gate in every excluded family, with mean difference -0.0304. Its family-weighted share of series with more than 5% added error was 20.5%, versus 3.9% for the gate. The earlier median-skill score also favoured the gate. The exact two-sided family sign-flip p was 0.0625; grouping the three German families gave p = 0.25. Selected crop-yield and invertebrate series had positive predicted advantage but negative observed advantage. Thus these four diagnostics did not recover useful subsets better than the family gate in this test. This is a retrospective comparison with known source summaries, observed weather and only three main final data sources. It is not a prospective or operational validation. Code, exact published model statistics, fitted rules, all decisions and an independent arithmetic audit are included.

display.caption: The four-diagnostic rule lost to the trend-aware family gate in all five excluded families. Whole-family holdouts, rather than random series splits, test transfer. The score is bounded relative error advantage; zero is the trailing mean.
